newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai rubber prices mostly steady, trade slow.
newsitem.headline: Thai rubber prices mostly steady, trade slow.

text.p: Thai rubber prices were mostly steady despite market talk that the government bought more than 4,000 tonnes of rubber under its intervention plan, trade sources said on Friday.
But officials refused to confirm or deny the report.
The market was quiet, with bids far outnumbered by offers, and deals were modest. Buyers from the United States were absent from the market, trade sources said.
They said Thailand was close to inking a deal to sell 20,000 tonnes of rubber to the Netherlands for US$1,260 per tonne on an FOB basis.
Under the deal, Thailand would in turn buy up to 500,000 tonnes of fertiliser from the country.
"It's such a quiet day. The price could head lower if demand next week is bearish like this despite the government price intervention scheme," he said.
Although the government's programme was aimed primarily at helping rubber planters by boosting local prices, it was also expected to pull up offer prices.
Under the scheme, the government will buy RSS3 grade rubber at 27.50 baht a kg ($1.05) from 25.00 baht previously.
The government would also provide one billion baht of soft loans for operating funds and 1.5 billion baht for export supporting funds for the industry.
Other dealers said any downside would be limited as tighter supplies during the wintering season should support the price.
The amount of rubber entering the market this week dropped by 20 percent to 125,123 kg.
Thai benchmark RSS3 for April delivery was quoted around 122-12.50 US cents a kg FOB Bangkok while concentrated latex was quoted around 94 cents a kg.
